Calling .toString() on a Zod instance yields '[object Object]', so the schema becomes {access_token, "[object Object]": number}, not a wildcard. In sync mode (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set), safeParse strips all non-declared fields, so only access_token survives; expiry fields (expiry_date/expires_in) are dropped, causing undefined/NaN downstream in expiry logic (e.g., GoogleCalendarService sets googleCredentials.expiry_date from token.expiry_date). This is a real correctness defect introduced by the new file.

judged_text: The minimumTokenResponseSchema catch-all keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the string "[object Object]" (Object.prototype.toString on a Zod instance), so the schema is `{access_token, "[object Object]"}` and the intended 'any numeric property is the expiry' wildcard never matches; zod's default stripping then drops every field except access_token. In sync mode the parsed token response contains only access_token — expiry_date/expires_in and any other fields are silently stripped, so downstream expiry computations get undefined/NaN even once the Response-shape bug is fixed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions are evaluated immediately to a single string key (very likely `"[object Object]"`), not a wildcard/catch-all. The second computed key also overwrites the first, so the schema effectively becomes `{ access_token, "[object Object]"?: ... }` and, because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, real token fields like `expiry_date`, `expires_in`, etc. will be dropped in the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` path. This matches the finding that sync-mode parsing can silently lose expiry-related fields.
